records.literal_gloss: After these things was a feast of the Jews, and went up Jesus to Jerusalem.

en.L: After these things there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
en.B: Some time after this there was a Jewish festival, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
en.R: Later on it was time for one of the Jewish festivals, so Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

es.L: Después de estas cosas había una fiesta de los judíos, y Jesús subió a Jerusalén.
es.B: Algún tiempo después hubo una fiesta judía, y Jesús subió a Jerusalén.
es.R: Más tarde llegó una de las fiestas judías, así que Jesús subió a Jerusalén.

fr.L: Après ces choses, il y avait une fête des Juifs, et Jésus monta à Jérusalem.
fr.B: Quelque temps après, il y eut une fête juive, et Jésus monta à Jérusalem.
fr.R: Plus tard, c’était le moment d’une des fêtes juives. Alors Jésus est monté à Jérusalem.

sw.L: Baada ya hayo ilikuwako sikukuu moja ya Wayahudi, na Yesu akapanda Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Muda fulani baada ya hayo kulikuwa na sikukuu ya Kiyahudi, na Yesu alipanda kwenda Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Baadaye ulifika wakati wa sikukuu moja ya Wayahudi, kwa hiyo Yesu alipanda kwenda Yerusalemu.

vi.L: Sau những việc ấy, có một kỳ lễ của người Do Thái, và Đức Giê-xu lên Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: Ít lâu sau, có một kỳ lễ của người Do Thái, và Đức Giê-xu lên Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: Sau đó, đến kỳ một lễ hội của người Do Thái, nên Đức Giê-xu lên Giê-ru-sa-lem.

ko.L: 이 일들 후에 유대인의 명절이 있어서, 예수께서 예루살렘으로 올라가셨다.
ko.B: 얼마 뒤에 유대인의 명절이 되어, 예수께서 예루살렘으로 올라가셨다.
ko.R: 얼마 후에 유대인의 명절 가운데 하나가 다가왔다. 그래서 예수께서 예루살렘으로 올라가셨다.

decisions.choice: a feast, without the article (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the feast, with the article (some important manuscripts, among them Codex Sinaiticus)
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts read "the feast of the Jews". With the article the phrase would most naturally point to a well-known festival, either Passover or the Feast of Tabernacles. Without it, John leaves the festival unnamed. A footnote gives the other reading. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: an unnamed festival; John does not say which
decisions.reason: Elsewhere John names the festivals: Passover (2:13; 6:4; 11:55), Tabernacles (7:2) and Dedication (10:22). Here he does not, and the story does not depend on which one it was. Many Jews went up to Jerusalem for the pilgrim festivals (Deuteronomy 16:16), which is why there were crowds in the city (verse 13).

decisions.choice: the Jews: the Jewish people, whose festival it was
decisions.reason: As at 2:13, John names the festival as the people's, for readers who did not keep it. Jesus goes up to keep it as a Jew himself.

decisions.choice: went up: the usual way of speaking of travel to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Jerusalem stands high in the hill country of Judea, and pilgrims always "went up" to it, whatever direction they came from (2:13; Psalm 122:4).

decisions.choice: a Jewish festival (B); one of the Jewish festivals (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the Jewish people (meaning decision m3), so Balanced and Readable say "Jewish" without naming the leaders. "Festival" is the everyday word for a feast day of this kind.

decisions.choice: it was time for ... so
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that Jesus went to Jerusalem because of the festival, which the sentence implies.

decisions.choice: una fiesta judía (B); una de las fiestas judías (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the Jewish people, whose festival it was (meaning decision m3), so no level speaks of leaders.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense ("dit", "trouve"); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
the present tense throughout at Literal
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (5:1-18). The passé simple ("monta", "répondit") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Literal uses it for the Greek past tenses and keeps the present where John tells a past event in the present (5:6 and 5:8 "dit", 5:14 "trouve"), as the English Literal does. Readable uses the passé composé ("Jésus est monté"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. Inside speech every level uses the passé composé ("celui qui m’a guéri"). The imperfect ("gisaient", "persécutaient") is used at every level for what was usual or going on.

decisions.choice: des Juifs (L); juive, juives (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the Jewish people, whose festival it was (meaning decision m3), so Balanced and Readable say "juive" and do not name the leaders, as they do from 5:10 on.

source.text: ἔστιν δὲ ἐν τοῖς Ἱεροσολύμοις ἐπὶ τῇ προβατικῇ κολυμβήθρα ἡ ἐπιλεγομένη Ἑβραϊστὶ Βηθεσδά, πέντε στοὰς ἔχουσα·

records.literal_gloss: There is now in the Jerusalem by the sheep [gate] a pool, the [one] being called in Hebrew Bethesda, five colonnades having;

en.L: Now there is in Jerusalem, by the Sheep [Gate], a pool which is called in Hebrew Bethesda, having five porticoes.
en.B: In Jerusalem, by the Sheep Gate, there is a pool with five porticoes; in Hebrew it is called Bethesda.
en.R: In Jerusalem, near the gate called the Sheep Gate, there is a pool. In the Hebrew language it is called Bethesda. It has five porches with roofs.

es.L: Y hay en Jerusalén, junto a la [puerta] de las Ovejas, un estanque llamado en hebreo Betesda, que tiene cinco pórticos.
es.B: En Jerusalén, junto a la puerta de las Ovejas, hay un estanque con cinco pórticos; en hebreo se llama Betesda.
es.R: En Jerusalén, cerca de la puerta llamada de las Ovejas, hay un estanque. En idioma hebreo se llama Betesda. Tiene cinco corredores con techo.

fr.L: Or il y a à Jérusalem, près de la [porte] des Brebis, une piscine appelée en hébreu Béthesda, qui a cinq portiques.
fr.B: À Jérusalem, près de la porte des Brebis, il y a un bassin entouré de cinq portiques ; on l’appelle en hébreu Béthesda.
fr.R: À Jérusalem, près de la porte qu’on appelle la porte des Brebis, il y a un bassin. En langue hébraïque, on l’appelle Béthesda. Il est entouré de cinq galeries couvertes.

sw.L: Basi kuna huko Yerusalemu, karibu na [Lango la] Kondoo, bwawa liitwalo kwa Kiebrania Bethesda, lenye matao matano.
sw.B: Huko Yerusalemu, karibu na Lango la Kondoo, kuna bwawa lenye matao matano; kwa Kiebrania linaitwa Bethesda.
sw.R: Huko Yerusalemu, karibu na lango liitwalo Lango la Kondoo, kuna bwawa la maji. Kwa lugha ya Kiebrania linaitwa Bethesda. Lina vibaraza vitano vyenye paa.

vi.L: Bấy giờ tại Giê-ru-sa-lem, gần [Cửa] Chiên, có một cái hồ, tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ gọi là Bê-tết-đa, có năm dãy hành lang.
vi.B: Tại Giê-ru-sa-lem, gần Cửa Chiên, có một cái hồ với năm dãy hành lang có cột; tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ gọi là Bê-tết-đa.
vi.R: Ở Giê-ru-sa-lem, gần cổng gọi là Cửa Chiên, có một cái hồ. Tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ gọi hồ ấy là Bê-tết-đa. Hồ có năm dãy hiên có mái che.

ko.L: 그런데 예루살렘에는 양 [문] 곁에 히브리 말로 베데스다라고 하는 못이 있는데, 회랑 다섯이 있다.
ko.B: 예루살렘의 양 문 곁에는 회랑이 다섯 있는 못이 있는데, 히브리 말로 베데스다라고 한다.
ko.R: 예루살렘에 있는 양 문이라는 문 가까이에 연못이 하나 있다. 그 연못은 히브리 말로 베데스다라고 한다. 그곳에는 지붕이 있는 복도가 다섯 개 있다.

decisions.choice: by the Sheep Gate there is a pool
alternatives: by the sheep pool there is a place called Bethesda
by the sheep market there is a pool
decisions.reason: The word for "sheep" is an adjective with no noun, so a noun has to be understood. Nehemiah names a Sheep Gate in the north wall of Jerusalem, near the temple (Nehemiah 3:1, 32; 12:39), and that is the most natural noun to supply. Some manuscripts have the word for "pool" in a different case, which would give "by the sheep pool", with Bethesda as the name of the place around it. The KJV's "sheep market" supplies a noun the text does not suggest.

decisions.choice: Bethesda (SBLGNT)
decisions.reason: The manuscripts spell the name in several ways. Bethesda is found in many manuscripts of different kinds; Bethzatha in Codex Sinaiticus and a few others; Bethsaida in some early manuscripts, though that is the name of a town in Galilee (1:44). Bethzatha was also the name of a district just north of the temple, where the pool lay. A copper scroll found at Qumran appears to name a place with pools in Jerusalem by a form close to Bethesda. The evidence is evenly balanced; a footnote gives the other spellings. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: in Hebrew: in the language of the Jews of the land
decisions.reason: John uses this word for the local language of Judea (19:13, 17, 20; 20:16). In daily speech that was mostly Aramaic, a language close to Hebrew, and names such as this one could be either. The meaning of the name is uncertain; "house of mercy" and "house of the outpouring" have both been suggested.

decisions.choice: five porticoes: covered walkways with columns
decisions.reason: A portico is a roofed walkway open on one side, with a row of columns. Digging near the Church of St Anne in Jerusalem has uncovered two large pools side by side, separated by a wall of rock, which fits five porticoes: one on each of the four sides and one across the middle.

decisions.choice: there is: a present tense describing the place
decisions.reason: John says the pool "is" there. Writers often describe a place in the present, so the tense need not mean the pool was still standing when John wrote; it does show that he knew the place well.

decisions.choice: Sheep [Gate] (L); Sheep Gate (B, R)
decisions.reason: Every level supplies "Gate" (meaning decision m1); Literal shows it in brackets.

decisions.choice: porticoes (L, B); porches with roofs (R)
decisions.reason: "Portico" is the exact word for a roofed walkway with columns; Readable describes it in plain words.

decisions.choice: in Hebrew
decisions.reason: Keeps the word John used; meaning decision m3 explains which language this was.

decisions.choice: la [puerta] de las Ovejas
decisions.reason: As in English: every level supplies "puerta" (meaning decision m1); Literal shows it in brackets.

decisions.choice: pórticos (L, B); corredores con techo (R)
decisions.reason: "Pórtico" is the exact word for a roofed walkway with columns; Readable describes it in plain words.

decisions.choice: une piscine (L); un bassin (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a pool for bathing or for water. French "piscine" is the traditional word and is kept at Literal, but today it first means a swimming pool; "bassin" gives Balanced and Readable the right picture of a stone pool. The same choice holds for 5:7.

decisions.choice: Béthesda
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads Bethesda here (meaning decision m2, whose footnote gives the other readings); "Béthesda" is its usual French spelling. A shared list for the French of John had proposed "Bethzatha", which is a variant reading, not the text translated.

decisions.choice: portiques (L, B); galeries couvertes (R)
decisions.reason: "Portique" is the exact word for a roofed walkway on columns; Readable describes it in plain words, as "la galerie couverte appelée portique de Salomon" does at 10:23.

decisions.choice: matao (L, B); vibaraza vyenye paa (R)
decisions.reason: The porticoes were covered walkways with columns. "Matao" (arcades) is the standard word for them; Readable says "vibaraza vyenye paa" (porches with roofs), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ"
decisions.reason: The established Protestant name for the language; it covers the language of the Jews of the land, as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: "회랑" (L, B); "지붕이 있는 복도" (R)
decisions.reason: "회랑" is the current word for a roofed colonnade; "행각" is the older Bible word and is unclear to most readers today.

source.text: ἐν ταύταις κατέκειτο πλῆθος τῶν ἀσθενούντων, τυφλῶν, χωλῶν, ξηρῶν.

records.literal_gloss: In these were lying a multitude of the being sick, blind, lame, withered.

en.L: In these lay a multitude of the sick, blind, lame, withered.
en.B: Many sick people used to lie in these porticoes: the blind, the lame and the paralyzed.
en.R: Lots of sick people would lie there in the porches. Some were blind, some could not walk well, and some had arms or legs they could not move.

es.L: En estos yacía una multitud de enfermos, ciegos, cojos, tullidos.
es.B: Muchos enfermos solían estar tendidos en esos pórticos: ciegos, cojos y paralíticos.
es.R: Mucha gente enferma solía estar acostada allí, en los corredores. Algunos eran ciegos, otros no podían caminar bien y otros tenían brazos o piernas que no podían mover.

fr.L: Sous ceux-ci gisait une multitude de malades, d’aveugles, de boiteux, de paralysés.
fr.B: Sous ces portiques, de nombreux malades restaient couchés : des aveugles, des boiteux et des paralysés.
fr.R: Beaucoup de malades restaient couchés là, sous les galeries. Certains étaient aveugles, d’autres avaient du mal à marcher, et d’autres avaient des bras ou des jambes qu’ils ne pouvaient plus bouger.

sw.L: Ndani ya hayo walilala wagonjwa wengi, vipofu, viwete, waliopooza.
sw.B: Wagonjwa wengi walikuwa wakilala katika matao hayo: vipofu, viwete na waliopooza.
sw.R: Wagonjwa wengi walikuwa wakilala pale vibarazani. Wengine walikuwa vipofu, wengine hawakuweza kutembea vizuri, na wengine walikuwa na mikono au miguu isiyoweza kusogea.

vi.L: Trong các hành lang ấy có rất nhiều người bệnh nằm: người mù, người què, người bại.
vi.B: Nhiều người bệnh thường nằm trong các hành lang ấy: người mù, người què và người bại liệt.
vi.R: Rất nhiều người bệnh thường nằm ở các dãy hiên ấy. Có người bị mù, có người đi không được, có người bị liệt tay chân.

ko.L: 그 안에 많은 병자들, 곧 눈먼 사람들, 다리 저는 사람들, 몸이 마른 사람들이 누워 있었다.
ko.B: 이 회랑들에는 많은 병자들이 누워 있곤 했다. 눈먼 사람, 다리를 저는 사람, 몸이 마비된 사람들이었다.
ko.R: 그 복도에는 아픈 사람들이 많이 누워 있곤 했다. 눈이 보이지 않는 사람도 있었고, 잘 걷지 못하는 사람도 있었고, 팔이나 다리를 움직이지 못하는 사람도 있었다.

decisions.choice: the verse ends here; the words about the angel stirring the water (verses 3b-4) are not part of the text
alternatives: "... withered, waiting for the moving of the water. For an angel went down at certain times into the pool and stirred the water; whoever stepped in first after the stirring of the water was made well of whatever disease he had."
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add that the sick were waiting for the water to move, and then explain why: from time to time an angel came down into the pool and stirred up the water, and the first person to get into the water after it was stirred was healed, whatever the disease. The oldest manuscripts, among them two early papyri, Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, do not have these words. Some manuscripts have only part of them, others mark them as doubtful, and the wording varies a good deal from copy to copy. They seem to have been added to explain the sick man's words in verse 7. The SBLGNT does not print them, so verse 4 is not in the text and the numbering passes from verse 3 to verse 5. A footnote gives the added words. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: withered: with limbs shrunken or paralyzed
decisions.reason: The word means dry or withered. Used of people, as of the man with the "withered" hand (Mark 3:1-3), it describes limbs that have wasted and cannot be used.

decisions.choice: lay: the imperfect describes what was usual there
alternatives: were lying there on that one day
decisions.reason: The tense pictures a lasting scene: the porticoes were a place where sick people regularly lay, hoping to be healed (verse 7).

decisions.choice: used to lie, paralyzed (B); would lie, arms or legs they could not move (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that this was the usual scene (meaning decision m3) and say in plain words what "withered" meant (m2).

decisions.choice: tullidos (L); solían estar tendidos, paralíticos (B); brazos o piernas que no podían mover (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable show that this was the usual scene (meaning decision m3) and say in plain words what "withered" meant (m2). Literal's "tullidos" keeps the old word for crippled limbs.

decisions.choice: paralysés (L, B)
decisions.reason: The Greek word, "dry" or "withered", is used of limbs shrunken or paralysed (meaning decision m2). French "desséché" said of a person sounds strange, and "impotent" now has another sense; "paralysés" is the plain word for those who could not move a limb, and Readable describes it.

source.text: ἦν δέ τις ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖ τριάκοντα ὀκτὼ ἔτη ἔχων ἐν τῇ ἀσθενείᾳ αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: Was now a certain man there thirty eight years having in the weakness of him;

en.L: Now a certain man was there who had been thirty-eight years in his illness.
en.B: One man there had been ill for thirty-eight years.
en.R: One of the men lying there had been sick for thirty-eight years.

es.L: Y estaba allí cierto hombre que llevaba treinta y ocho años en su enfermedad.
es.B: Había allí un hombre que llevaba treinta y ocho años enfermo.
es.R: Uno de los que estaban allí acostados llevaba treinta y ocho años enfermo.

fr.L: Or il y avait là un certain homme qui était dans sa maladie depuis trente-huit ans.
fr.B: Il y avait là un homme malade depuis trente-huit ans.
fr.R: Parmi les gens couchés là, il y avait un homme qui était malade depuis trente-huit ans.

sw.L: Basi palikuwa na mtu mmoja huko aliyekuwa na miaka thelathini na minane katika ugonjwa wake.
sw.B: Mtu mmoja pale alikuwa mgonjwa kwa miaka thelathini na minane.
sw.R: Mmoja wa watu waliolala pale alikuwa mgonjwa kwa miaka thelathini na minane.

vi.L: Bấy giờ ở đó có một người đã mang bệnh ba mươi tám năm.
vi.B: Ở đó có một người đã bị bệnh ba mươi tám năm.
vi.R: Trong số những người nằm đó, có một người đã bị bệnh ba mươi tám năm.

ko.L: 그런데 거기에 서른여덟 해 동안 병을 앓아 온 어떤 사람이 있었다.
ko.B: 거기에 서른여덟 해 동안 병을 앓고 있는 사람이 하나 있었다.
ko.R: 거기 누워 있는 사람들 가운데 서른여덟 해 동안 아팠던 사람이 있었다.

decisions.choice: having thirty-eight years in his illness: he had been ill for thirty-eight years
decisions.reason: To "have" a length of time in a state is a common way of saying how long it has lasted (compare verse 6, and 8:57; 11:17). The illness had lasted most of an ordinary lifetime. John does not name it, but verse 7 shows that he could not move quickly.

decisions.choice: thirty-eight years: a length of time, with no further meaning drawn from it
alternatives: an echo of the thirty-eight years Israel spent in the wilderness (Deuteronomy 2:14)
decisions.reason: The number matches the years of Israel's wandering after the spies' report (Deuteronomy 2:14), and some readers see a picture of Israel in the man. John draws no such link, and the number fits a plain report of a long illness.

decisions.choice: One of the men lying there
decisions.reason: Readable ties the man to the sick people of verse 3.

decisions.choice: llevaba treinta y ocho años
decisions.reason: Spanish "llevar" + a length of time is the same idiom as the Greek "having" (meaning decision m1), so every level can keep it.

source.text: τοῦτον ἰδὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς κατακείμενον, καὶ γνοὺς ὅτι πολὺν ἤδη χρόνον ἔχει, λέγει αὐτῷ· Θέλεις ὑγιὴς γενέσθαι;

records.literal_gloss: This [one] having seen the Jesus lying, and having known that much already time he has, says to him, "Do you want well to become?"

en.L: When Jesus saw this [man] lying [there] and knew that he had already been [so] a long time, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says to him, "Do you want to become well?"
en.B: Jesus saw him lying there and knew that he had been in that condition for a long time, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked him, "Do you want to be well?"
en.R: Jesus saw the man lying there. He knew that the man had been sick for a long time. So Jesus asked him, "Would you like to get well?"

es.L: Jesús, al verlo tendido y saber que llevaba ya mucho tiempo [así], le dice: «¿Quieres quedar sano?».
es.B: Jesús lo vio tendido allí y supo que llevaba mucho tiempo en esa situación, así que le preguntó: «¿Quieres quedar sano?».
es.R: Jesús vio al hombre acostado allí. Supo que llevaba mucho tiempo enfermo. Entonces le preguntó: «¿Te gustaría quedar sano?».

fr.L: Quand Jésus vit celui-ci couché [là] et sut qu’il était [ainsi] depuis déjà longtemps, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « Veux-tu devenir bien portant ? »
fr.B: Jésus le vit couché là et apprit qu’il était dans cet état depuis longtemps ; alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui demanda : « Veux-tu guérir ? »
fr.R: Jésus a vu l’homme couché là. Il a appris que l’homme était malade depuis longtemps. Alors Jésus lui a demandé : « Est-ce que tu veux guérir ? »

sw.L: Yesu alipomwona huyu amelala [hapo], na kujua kwamba amekuwa [hivyo] muda mrefu tayari, anamwambia, "Je, unataka kupata kuwa mzima?"
sw.B: Yesu alimwona amelala pale, akajua kwamba alikuwa katika hali hiyo kwa muda mrefu, basi akamwuliza, "Je, unataka kuwa mzima?"
sw.R: Yesu alimwona yule mtu amelala pale. Alijua kwamba mtu huyo alikuwa mgonjwa kwa muda mrefu. Basi Yesu akamwuliza, "Ungependa kupona?"

vi.L: Đức Giê-xu thấy người này nằm [đó] và biết rằng ông đã [như vậy] lâu ngày, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với ông: "Ông có muốn được lành không?"
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu thấy ông nằm đó và biết ông đã bị như vậy lâu ngày, nên {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hỏi: "Ông có muốn được lành không?"

ko.L: 예수께서 이 [사람이] 누워 있는 것을 보시고, 그가 이미 오랫동안 [그렇게] 지냈다는 것을 아시고 그에게 말씀하신다. "건강하게 되기를 원하느냐?"
ko.B: 예수께서 그가 누워 있는 것을 보시고, 그가 오랫동안 그런 상태로 지냈다는 것을 아시고 물으셨다. "낫고 싶으냐?"
ko.R: 예수께서 그 사람이 누워 있는 것을 보셨다. 예수께서는 그가 오랫동안 아팠다는 것을 아셨다. 그래서 그에게 물으셨다. "병이 낫고 싶으냐?"

decisions.choice: knew, having learned it; John does not say how
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to come to know as well as to know. Jesus may have been told, or seen it for himself; John shows him knowing what others have not told him elsewhere (1:47-48; 2:24-25; 4:17-18), but here he does not say which.

decisions.choice: Jesus takes the first step and asks the man what he wants
alternatives: a question that doubts the man's wish to be healed
decisions.reason: The man does not ask Jesus for anything; Jesus comes to him. The question is not idle: it draws the man's attention from the pool to the one speaking with him. His answer (verse 7) shows that he can think only of the water.

decisions.choice: well: whole, sound in body
decisions.reason: The word means healthy or whole. It runs through the story (verses 6, 9, 11, 14, 15) and is taken up again in 7:23, where Jesus speaks of having made "a whole man well" on the Sabbath.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Christ uses the deity_pronoun setting, including "you" when people speak to him. At the start of a sentence "He" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: asked (B, R); also told (verse 8) and found (verse 14)
decisions.reason: John often tells a story in the present tense ("he says") for vividness. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as stories are normally told in this language. This applies to every such verb in the passage (verses 6, 8 and 14).

decisions.choice: well
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the same word each time it comes in the story (meaning decision m3), so that the repeated word stays visible.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present ("le dice", "lo encuentra"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: sano
decisions.reason: Every level keeps the same word each time it comes in the story (verses 6, 9, 11, 14, 15), so the repetition stays visible (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: bien portant (L); guérir, guéri (B, R)
decisions.reason: The same Greek word for "well" comes back in 5:9, 5:11, 5:14 and 5:15 (meaning decision m3). Literal renders it each time with "bien portant", which says sound in body and stays distinct from the verbs for healing in 5:10 and 5:13. Balanced and Readable use "guérir" and "guéri", the everyday words, at every occurrence, so the repetition stays visible there too.

decisions.choice: kuwa mzima (L, B); kupona (R)
decisions.reason: ὑγιὴς is whole, sound in body. "Mzima" means both healthy and whole, so it serves the word each time it comes back in this chapter (verses 9, 11, 14, 15). Readable says "kupona" (get well) where the English Readable says "get well".

decisions.choice: historic present: Literal "nói" without "đã"; the other levels tell it as past where Vietnamese needs it
decisions.reason: Vietnamese verbs do not mark tense, so John's historic present shows only in Literal leaving out "đã"; one decision for the passage.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans; "께서" and the honorific "-시-" carry the respect
alternatives: a deity_pronoun span around "그분" (it would have nothing to change)
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change and the Korean text has no such spans in this passage. Jesus speaks in 해라체 to the man and to his opponents, as the guide sets.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal ("말씀하신다", "찾아내신다"); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As the guide asks, Literal keeps John's present tense in narrative; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past. One decision for the passage.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη αὐτῷ ὁ ἀσθενῶν· Κύριε, ἄνθρωπον οὐκ ἔχω ἵνα ὅταν ταραχθῇ τὸ ὕδωρ βάλῃ με εἰς τὴν κολυμβήθραν· ἐν ᾧ δὲ ἔρχομαι ἐγὼ ἄλλος πρὸ ἐμοῦ καταβαίνει.

records.literal_gloss: Answered him the being sick, "Sir, a man not I have that when is stirred the water he may put me into the pool; in which [time] but am coming I, another before me goes down."

en.L: The sick [man] answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Sir, I do not have a {{gender:person|man}} to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up; but while I am coming, another goes down before me."
en.B: The sick man answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Sir, when the water is stirred up, there is no one to put me into the pool. And while I am on my way, someone else steps down before I do."
en.R: The sick man answered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Sir, there is no one to help me get into the pool when the water starts to move. While I am trying to get there, someone else always gets in first."

es.L: Le respondió el enfermo: «Señor, no tengo {{gender:a nadie|un hombre}} que me meta en el estanque cuando se agita el agua; y mientras yo voy, otro baja antes que yo».
es.B: El enfermo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondió: «Señor, cuando se agita el agua, no hay nadie que me meta en el estanque. Y mientras voy, otro baja antes que yo».
es.R: El enfermo {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} respondió: «Señor, no tengo a nadie que me ayude a meterme en el estanque cuando el agua empieza a moverse. Mientras trato de llegar, siempre se mete otro antes que yo».

fr.L: Le malade {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondit : « Monsieur, je n’ai {{gender:personne|pas d’homme}} pour me jeter dans la piscine quand l’eau est agitée ; et pendant que moi, j’y vais, un autre descend avant moi. »
fr.B: Le malade {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} répondit : « Monsieur, quand l’eau se met à bouger, je n’ai personne pour me plonger dans le bassin. Et le temps que j’y aille, un autre descend avant moi. »
fr.R: Le malade {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a répondu : « Monsieur, je n’ai personne pour m’aider à entrer dans le bassin quand l’eau commence à bouger. Pendant que j’essaie d’y aller, quelqu’un d’autre y entre toujours avant moi. »

sw.L: Yule mgonjwa akamjibu, "Sina mtu, bwana, wa kunitumbukiza bwawani maji yanapovurugwa; na ninapokuwa nakuja, mwingine hushuka kabla yangu."
sw.B: Yule mgonjwa akamjibu, "Maji yanapovurugwa, bwana, sina mtu wa kuniingiza bwawani. Na ninapojaribu kwenda, mtu mwingine hushuka kabla yangu."
sw.R: Yule mgonjwa akamjibu, "Hakuna mtu wa kunisaidia, bwana, kuingia bwawani maji yanapoanza kuchafuka. Ninapojaribu kufika huko, mtu mwingine huingia kwanza kila mara."

vi.L: Người bệnh trả lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa ông, tôi không có ai để đưa tôi xuống hồ khi nước động; nhưng trong lúc tôi đang đến, thì có người khác xuống trước tôi."
vi.B: Người bệnh thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa ông, khi nước động thì không có ai đưa tôi xuống hồ. Trong lúc tôi đang lết tới, thì người khác đã xuống trước tôi rồi."
vi.R: Người bệnh trả lời {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa ông, khi nước bắt đầu động, không có ai giúp tôi xuống hồ. Trong lúc tôi cố lết tới đó, thì lúc nào cũng có người khác xuống trước."

ko.L: 그 병자가 그분께 대답했다. "선생님, 물이 휘저어질 때 저를 못에 넣어 줄 사람이 없습니다. 제가 가는 동안에 다른 사람이 저보다 먼저 내려갑니다."
ko.B: 그 병자가 대답했다. "선생님, 물이 출렁일 때 저를 못에 넣어 줄 사람이 없습니다. 제가 가는 사이에 다른 사람이 먼저 내려가 버립니다."
ko.R: 그 병자가 대답했다. "선생님, 물이 움직이기 시작할 때 저를 연못에 넣어 줄 사람이 없습니다. 제가 그곳으로 가려고 애쓰는 동안 언제나 다른 사람이 먼저 들어갑니다."

decisions.choice: Sir: a polite address to a man he does not know
alternatives: Lord, a confession of who Jesus is
decisions.reason: The word is the one later used of Jesus as Lord (20:28), but it was also the ordinary courteous way to address a man. This man does not know who Jesus is (verse 13). A footnote gives "Lord".

decisions.choice: when the water is stirred: the sick believed that the first one into the water after it moved would be healed
alternatives: John himself teaches that the water healed
decisions.reason: The man speaks of a belief held by those who waited at the pool: from time to time the water was disturbed, perhaps by a spring or by water let in from another pool, and the first one in was thought to be healed. John reports what the man believed; he does not say whether it was so. The words added in some manuscripts after verse 3 explain the belief (see the note there).

decisions.choice: a man: anyone at all to help him
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary one for a person, and here it means he has no one at all. It also sets up the contrast of the story: the man who has no one to help him is found by Jesus.

decisions.choice: while I am coming, another goes down: what happens each time
decisions.reason: The present tenses describe what keeps happening: he is too slow, and every time someone else gets in first.

decisions.choice: Sir
decisions.reason: Shows the polite address (meaning decision m1); "Lord" would put in his mouth a confession he has not made.

decisions.choice: a {{gender:person|man}}
decisions.reason: The word means a person of either sex (meaning decision m3), so Literal gives the inclusive word by default and "man" as the alternative. Balanced and Readable say "no one", which needs no setting.

decisions.choice: always
decisions.reason: Readable shows that this keeps happening (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: Señor
decisions.reason: As at 4:11: Spanish "señor" is both the polite "sir" and "Lord", so it keeps the man's word without making him confess what he does not know (meaning decision m1). Here it is the polite address; it is capitalized only because it begins his speech.

decisions.choice: {{gender:a nadie|un hombre}}
decisions.reason: The word means a person of either sex (meaning decision m3). Literal gives the inclusive "a nadie" by default and the traditional "un hombre" as the alternative; Balanced and Readable say "nadie".

decisions.choice: Monsieur
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: the man does not know who Jesus is (meaning decision m1), so he says "Monsieur", the polite French address to a stranger; the footnote on m1 gives "Seigneur".

decisions.choice: je n’ai {{gender:personne|pas d’homme}} (L)
alternatives: je n’ai pas d’homme, with no setting
decisions.reason: The word means anyone at all (meaning decision m3). French "personne" is already inclusive, so the default reads "je n’ai personne"; the traditional alternative keeps the Greek word "homme". Balanced and Readable say "personne" and need no setting.

decisions.choice: bwana, placed inside the sentence
decisions.reason: As in John 4: the man is addressing a stranger, so this is "sir", not "Lord". Placed after the first phrase, "bwana" stays lowercase and reads as "sir".

decisions.choice: sina mtu, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "a man" as the traditional alternative to "a person". "Mtu" already means anyone, man or woman, so Swahili needs no span here or in verses 34 and 41.

decisions.choice: the man says "Thưa ông" and "tôi"; Jesus calls him "ông"
decisions.reason: He does not know who Jesus is (5:13), so "kyrie" is the polite address to a man, as docs/john-terms.md sets out. Jesus and the others call him "ông": a grown man ill for thirty-eight years.

decisions.choice: "không có ai" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: "ai" (anyone) already includes men and women; the setting has nothing to change.

decisions.choice: "선생님" for kyrie; the man speaks in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: He does not know who Jesus is, so his "kyrie" is the polite "선생님"; the footnote gives "주님".

decisions.choice: "사람" with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean "사람" means anyone at all, man or woman, so the English gender span has no Korean counterpart.

source.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἔγειρε ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ περιπάτει.

en.L: Jesus says to him, "Rise, take up your mat, and walk."

es.B: Jesús le dijo: «Levántate, recoge tu camilla y echa a andar».
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «¡Levántate! ¡Toma tu camilla y camina!».

fr.B: Jésus lui dit : « Lève-toi, ramasse ta natte et mets-toi à marcher. »

ko.L: 예수께서 그에게 말씀하신다. "일어나 네 자리를 들고 걸어가라."
ko.B: 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "일어나서 네 자리를 들고 걸어가거라."
ko.R: 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "일어나라! 네 자리를 들고 걸어가라!"

decisions.choice: mat: a poor person's light bedding that could be rolled up and carried
decisions.reason: The word is a common one for the thin mattress or pallet that poorer people slept on. It was light enough to carry, as the paralyzed man's mat is in Mark 2:4-12.

decisions.choice: two commands for single acts, then one for going on: get up, take up, and walk about
decisions.reason: The first two commands are for single acts. The third, "walk", is in a form that describes ongoing action: he is to start walking and keep on. Jesus heals by his word alone, as with the official's son (4:50).

decisions.choice: start walking
decisions.reason: Shows that the command is to begin walking and keep on (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: mat
decisions.reason: "Bed" suggests furniture too heavy to carry; "mat" gives the right picture (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: camilla
decisions.reason: "Lecho" and "cama" suggest furniture too heavy to carry; "camilla" is the light bedding a man could roll up and carry (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: echa a andar
decisions.reason: Shows that the command is to begin walking and keep on (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: natte
decisions.reason: The Greek word is a poor man's light bedding that could be rolled up and carried (meaning decision m1). "Lit" suggests furniture, "grabat" is old-fashioned and suggests a wretched bed rather than one carried, and "brancard" needs two bearers; "natte" gives the picture of a mat he could roll up. The same word is used through 5:9-12.

decisions.choice: mkeka
decisions.reason: The meaning note describes a poor person's light bedding that could be rolled up and carried. "Mkeka" (a sleeping mat) is exactly that; "godoro" (mattress) and "kitanda" (bed) are too heavy for a man to pick up and walk off with.

decisions.choice: "chiếu" (mat)
decisions.reason: A poor man's bedding that rolls up and can be carried; "giường" (bed) would make the command sound impossible.

decisions.choice: "자리" for the mat
decisions.reason: "자리" is the plain word for a mat to lie on and fits a light bedding that can be rolled up and carried; "침상" suggests a bed with a frame.

source.text: καὶ εὐθέως ἐγένετο ὑγιὴς ὁ ἄνθρωπος καὶ ἦρε τὸν κράβαττον αὐτοῦ καὶ περιεπάτει.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately became well the man and took up the mat of him and was walking.

en.L: And immediately the man became well, and he took up his mat and was walking.

en.R: Right away the man was well! He picked up his mat and started walking.

es.R: ¡En ese mismo momento el hombre quedó sano! Recogió su camilla y empezó a caminar.

fr.L: Et aussitôt l’homme devint bien portant, et il prit sa natte, et il marchait.
fr.B: Aussitôt l’homme fut guéri. Il ramassa sa natte et se mit à marcher.

sw.R: Papo hapo yule mtu akapona! Akachukua mkeka wake, akaanza kutembea.

vi.L: Lập tức người ấy được lành, vác chiếu mình lên và bước đi.
vi.B: Lập tức người ấy được lành. Ông vác chiếu lên và bắt đầu đi lại.
vi.R: Ngay lúc đó, người ấy được lành! Ông vác chiếu lên và bắt đầu bước đi.

ko.L: 그러자 곧 그 사람이 나아서, 자기 자리를 들고 걸어 다녔다.
ko.B: 그 사람은 곧 나았다. 그는 자기 자리를 들고 걷기 시작했다.
ko.R: 그 사람은 바로 나았다! 그는 자리를 들고 걷기 시작했다.

decisions.choice: the healing is immediate and complete, and the man does exactly what Jesus said
decisions.reason: The narrative repeats the words of the command (verse 8): he took up his mat and walked. A man who could not reach the water in time now walks, at Jesus's word alone. John calls such deeds signs (2:11; 4:54); this one leads into Jesus's words about the Son giving life (5:21).

decisions.choice: was walking: began to walk about
decisions.reason: The verb is imperfect, like the command in verse 8. It pictures him starting to walk and carrying on, which is how the authorities come to see him carrying the mat (verse 10).

decisions.choice: began walking about (B); started walking (R)
decisions.reason: Shows the beginning of an action that went on (meaning decision m2).

source.text: Ἦν δὲ σάββατον ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: Was now Sabbath on that the day.

en.L: Now it was Sabbath on that day.
en.B: And this happened on a Sabbath.
en.R: This happened on a Sabbath, the weekly day of rest.

es.R: Esto pasó en sábado, el día de descanso de cada semana.

fr.B: Et cela se passait un jour de sabbat.
fr.R: Cela s’est passé un jour de sabbat, le jour de repos de chaque semaine.

sw.B: Na jambo hili lilitokea siku ya Sabato.
sw.R: Hili lilitokea siku ya Sabato, siku ya mapumziko ya kila wiki.

vi.L: Bấy giờ ngày ấy là ngày Sa-bát.
vi.B: Việc này xảy ra vào ngày Sa-bát.
vi.R: Việc này xảy ra vào ngày Sa-bát, là ngày nghỉ hằng tuần.

ko.B: 그런데 이 일이 있었던 날은 안식일이었다.
ko.R: 그런데 그날은 안식일, 곧 한 주에 한 번 쉬는 날이었다.

decisions.choice: Sabbath: the seventh day, kept holy by resting from work
decisions.reason: God commanded Israel to do no work on the seventh day of the week, from sunset on Friday to sunset on Saturday (Exodus 20:8-11; Deuteronomy 5:12-15). Keeping the Sabbath marked the Jews out among the nations, and it was guarded with great care.

decisions.choice: a late remark that turns the story
decisions.reason: John mentions the day only after the healing is over, as he does in 9:14. The remark turns a healing story into a dispute: everything that follows (verses 10-18) is about the Sabbath.

decisions.choice: And this happened on a Sabbath (B, R)
alternatives: Now that day was a Sabbath
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable tie the remark to the healing just told, which is the point of placing it here (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: the weekly day of rest
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word for readers who do not know it (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: el día de descanso de cada semana
decisions.reason: Spanish "sábado" is also the everyday name for Saturday, so readers may miss that it was the day of rest; Readable explains it (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ἔλεγον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τῷ τεθεραπευμένῳ· Σάββατόν ἐστιν, καὶ οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἆραι τὸν κράβαττον.

records.literal_gloss: Were saying therefore the Jews to the [one] having been healed, "Sabbath it is, and not it is lawful for you to take up the mat."

en.L: So the Jews were saying to the [man] who had been healed, "It is Sabbath, and it is not lawful for you to carry the mat."
en.B: So the Jewish leaders kept telling the man who had been healed, "It is the Sabbath. It is against the law for you to carry your mat."
en.R: So the Jewish leaders spoke to the man who had been healed. "Today is the Sabbath!" they said. "The law does not allow you to carry your mat."

es.L: Decían, pues, los judíos al que había sido sanado: «Es sábado, y no te es lícito cargar la camilla».
es.B: Por eso los dirigentes judíos le decían al que había sido sanado: «Es sábado. La ley no te permite cargar tu camilla».
es.R: Entonces los dirigentes judíos hablaron con el hombre que había sido sanado. «¡Hoy es sábado!», le dijeron. «La ley no te permite cargar tu camilla».

fr.L: Les Juifs disaient donc à celui qui avait été guéri : « C’est sabbat, et il ne t’est pas permis de porter la natte. »
fr.B: Aussi les chefs juifs répétaient-ils à l’homme qui avait été guéri : « C’est le sabbat. La Loi t’interdit de porter ta natte. »
fr.R: Alors les chefs juifs sont venus parler à l’homme qui avait été guéri. « Aujourd’hui, c’est le sabbat ! » lui ont-ils dit. « La Loi ne te permet pas de porter ta natte. »

sw.L: Basi Wayahudi walikuwa wakimwambia yule aliyeponywa, "Ni Sabato, wala si halali kwako kubeba mkeka."
sw.B: Basi viongozi wa Wayahudi wakawa wakimwambia yule aliyeponywa, "Leo ni Sabato. Ni kinyume cha sheria kwako kubeba mkeka wako."
sw.R: Basi viongozi wa Wayahudi wakamwambia yule aliyeponywa, "Leo ni Sabato!" wakasema. "Sheria haikuruhusu kubeba mkeka wako."

vi.L: Vậy người Do Thái nói với người đã được chữa lành: "Đang là ngày Sa-bát, và ông không được phép vác chiếu."
vi.B: Vì vậy, các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái cứ nói với người đã được chữa lành: "Hôm nay là ngày Sa-bát. Luật pháp không cho phép ông vác chiếu."
vi.R: Vì vậy, các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái nói với người đã được chữa lành. Họ bảo: "Hôm nay là ngày Sa-bát! Luật pháp không cho ông vác chiếu."

ko.L: 그러므로 유대인들이 병이 나은 사람에게 말하였다. "안식일이다. 네가 자리를 드는 것은 허락되지 않는다."
ko.B: 그래서 유대 지도자들은 병이 나은 사람에게 거듭 말했다. "오늘은 안식일이다. 네가 자리를 들고 다니는 것은 율법에 어긋난다."
ko.R: 그래서 유대 지도자들이 병이 나은 사람에게 말했다. "오늘은 안식일이다! 율법에 따르면 너는 자리를 들고 다니면 안 된다."

decisions.choice: the Jews: the religious authorities in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: They speak with authority about what the Law allows, they question the man about who told him to break it (verse 12), and they go on to persecute Jesus and seek to kill him (verses 16, 18). That is the leadership, not the people as a whole: the healed man, the crowd and Jesus himself are all Jews.

decisions.choice: carrying a load on the Sabbath counted as work
decisions.reason: Through Jeremiah God forbade carrying a load out of one's house or through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath (Jeremiah 17:21-22), and Nehemiah stopped people bringing loads into the city on that day (Nehemiah 13:15-19). Later Jewish teaching, collected in the Mishnah about AD 200, lists carrying a thing from one place to another among the kinds of work forbidden on the Sabbath (Shabbat 7:2). By that rule, the man's mat was a load.

decisions.choice: were saying: they confronted him, perhaps more than once
decisions.reason: The verb is imperfect. It may simply set the scene of an exchange, or show them pressing the point.

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms). The footnote gives the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: against the law (B); the law does not allow (R)
decisions.reason: Says plainly what "not lawful" means: forbidden by the Law as they understood it (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los dirigentes judíos (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the religious authorities (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable name them, as at 1:19 and 2:18. The word John wrote is "los judíos".

decisions.choice: la ley no te permite
decisions.reason: Says plainly what "not lawful" means (meaning decision m2); Literal keeps "lícito".

decisions.choice: les Juifs (L); les chefs juifs (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John, first used for the authorities in this passage here and followed in 5:15, 5:16 and 5:18. Literal keeps the word John wrote. Balanced and Readable name the group the context shows (meaning decision m1): in French, "les Juifs" alone reads as the whole people, and the man who was healed was a Jew himself.

decisions.choice: La Loi t’interdit (B); La Loi ne te permet pas (R)
alternatives: Il ne t’est pas permis (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English, Balanced and Readable say plainly what "not lawful" means: forbidden by the Law of Moses as they read it (meaning decision m2). "La Loi" takes a capital as the Law of Moses.

decisions.choice: Wayahudi (L); viongozi wa Wayahudi (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in John 1: here the authorities are meant, so Balanced and Readable name them. The same holds in verses 15, 16 and 18.

decisions.choice: "người Do Thái" (L); "các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái" (B, R) in 5:10-18
decisions.reason: The style guide and docs/john-terms.md: Literal keeps the word John wrote; where the authorities are meant, Balanced and Readable name them.

decisions.choice: "유대인들" (L); "유대 지도자들" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As john-terms.md and the guide set: Literal keeps the word John wrote, and Balanced and Readable name the authorities, as the meaning decision reads it. The same holds in 5:15-18.

decisions.choice: the leaders speak down to the man in 해라체 ("-이다", "너"); he answers them in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: Officials confronting a poor man would not use honorifics to him; he speaks up to them, as the guide sets for speaking to superiors.

source.text: ὃς δὲ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς· Ὁ ποιήσας με ὑγιῆ ἐκεῖνός μοι εἶπεν Ἆρον τὸν κράβαττόν σου καὶ περιπάτει.

records.literal_gloss: He but answered them, "The [one] having made me well, that [one] to me said, 'Take up the mat of you and walk.'"

en.L: But he answered them, "The one who made me well, that [one] said to me, 'Take up your mat and walk.'"
en.B: But he answered them, "The one who made me well is the one who told me, 'Pick up your mat and start walking.'"
en.R: He answered, "The man who made me well told me, 'Take your mat with you and walk.'"

es.L: Pero él les respondió: «El que me sanó, ese me dijo: “Toma tu camilla y anda”».
es.B: Pero él les respondió: «El mismo que me sanó fue el que me dijo: “Recoge tu camilla y echa a andar”».
es.R: Él les respondió: «El hombre que me sanó me dijo: “Toma tu camilla y camina”».

fr.L: Mais il leur répondit : « Celui qui m’a rendu bien portant, celui-là m’a dit : “Prends ta natte et marche.” »
fr.B: Mais il leur répondit : « C’est celui qui m’a guéri qui m’a dit : “Ramasse ta natte et mets-toi à marcher.” »
fr.R: Il a répondu : « L’homme qui m’a guéri m’a dit : “Prends ta natte avec toi et marche.” »

sw.L: Lakini yeye akawajibu, "Yule aliyenifanya mzima, huyo ndiye aliyeniambia, 'Chukua mkeka wako, utembee.'"
sw.B: Lakini akawajibu, "Yule aliyenifanya mzima ndiye aliyeniambia, 'Chukua mkeka wako, uanze kutembea.'"
sw.R: Akajibu, "Mtu aliyeniponya aliniambia, 'Chukua mkeka wako, utembee.'"

vi.L: Nhưng ông trả lời họ: "Người đã chữa lành cho tôi, chính người ấy đã nói với tôi: 'Hãy vác chiếu của ông lên và đi.'"
vi.B: Nhưng ông trả lời họ: "Người đã chữa lành cho tôi chính là người đã bảo tôi: 'Hãy vác chiếu lên và bước đi.'"
vi.R: Ông trả lời: "Người đã chữa lành cho tôi bảo tôi: 'Hãy mang chiếu của ông theo mà đi.'"

ko.L: 그러나 그가 그들에게 대답했다. "저를 낫게 해 준 그 사람이 저에게 '네 자리를 들고 걸어가라' 하고 말했습니다."
ko.B: 그가 대답했다. "저를 낫게 해 준 바로 그 사람이 저에게 '네 자리를 들고 걸어가라' 하고 말했습니다."
ko.R: 그가 대답했다. "저를 낫게 해 준 사람이 저에게 '네 자리를 들고 걸어가라' 하고 말했습니다."

decisions.choice: that one: he points to his healer as the one responsible
decisions.reason: The man puts "the one who made me well" first and then repeats him with an emphatic "that one". He defends himself by pointing to the authority of the one who healed him: someone who could do that had the right to tell him what to do.

decisions.choice: made me well: the phrase recurs as a mark of what Jesus has done
decisions.reason: "The one who made me well" comes again in verse 15, and Jesus uses the same words in 7:23. The authorities ask about the command to carry the mat (verse 12); the man keeps speaking of the healing.

decisions.choice: The man who
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain word; the healed man does not yet know who Jesus is.

decisions.choice: el que me sanó
decisions.reason: The phrase recurs in verse 15 and in 7:23 (meaning decision m2), so it is kept the same. "Él" here is the healed man and has no setting.

decisions.choice: "그 사람이 ... 말했습니다": no honorific for Jesus in the man's words
decisions.reason: The man does not know who healed him (5:13) and speaks of him to the authorities as an ordinary man; the narrator still gives Jesus the honorific.

source.text: ἠρώτησαν οὖν αὐτόν· Τίς ἐστιν ὁ ἄνθρωπος ὁ εἰπών σοι· Ἆρον καὶ περιπάτει;

records.literal_gloss: They asked therefore him, "Who is the man the [one] having said to you, 'Take up and walk'?"

en.L: So they asked him, "Who is the man who said to you, 'Take [it] up and walk'?"
en.B: So they asked him, "Who is this man who told you to pick it up and walk?"
en.R: So they asked him, "Who is the man who told you to pick up your mat and walk?"

es.L: Le preguntaron, pues: «¿Quién es el hombre que te dijo: “Toma [la camilla] y anda”?».
es.B: Entonces le preguntaron: «¿Quién es ese hombre que te dijo que la recogieras y anduvieras?».
es.R: Entonces le preguntaron: «¿Quién es el hombre que te dijo que recogieras tu camilla y caminaras?».

fr.L: Ils lui demandèrent donc : « Qui est l’homme qui t’a dit : “Prends[-la] et marche” ? »
fr.B: Ils lui demandèrent donc : « Qui est cet homme qui t’a dit de la ramasser et de marcher ? »
fr.R: Alors ils lui ont demandé : « Qui est l’homme qui t’a dit de prendre ta natte et de marcher ? »

sw.L: Basi wakamwuliza, "Ni nani yule mtu aliyekuambia, 'Chukua [mkeka], utembee'?"
sw.B: Basi wakamwuliza, "Ni nani huyo mtu aliyekuambia uuchukue, utembee?"
sw.R: Basi wakamwuliza, "Ni nani yule mtu aliyekuambia uchukue mkeka wako na utembee?"

vi.L: Vậy họ hỏi ông: "Người đã nói với ông: 'Hãy vác [chiếu] lên và đi' là ai?"
vi.B: Vậy họ hỏi ông: "Người bảo ông vác chiếu lên mà đi là ai vậy?"
vi.R: Vậy họ hỏi ông: "Ai là người đã bảo ông vác chiếu lên mà đi?"

ko.L: 그러자 그들이 그에게 물었다. "너에게 '[그것을] 들고 걸어가라' 하고 말한 사람이 누구냐?"
ko.B: 그들이 물었다. "너에게 그것을 들고 걸어가라고 한 그 사람이 누구냐?"
ko.R: 그들이 물었다. "너에게 자리를 들고 걸어가라고 말한 사람이 누구냐?"

decisions.choice: they ask about the command, not the healing
decisions.reason: The man has spoken of the one who made him well; the authorities ask only who told him to carry his mat. Their concern is the breach of the Sabbath rule, not the healing.

decisions.choice: the man: an ordinary word, perhaps with a note of disdain
decisions.reason: "Man" is a plain word, but set against "the one who made me well" it may suggest they think of Jesus as just some fellow who told the man to break the Law.

decisions.choice: Take [it] up
decisions.reason: The Greek command has no object here; Literal supplies "it" in brackets.

decisions.choice: Toma [la camilla]
decisions.reason: As in English: the Greek command has no object here; Literal supplies it in brackets.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἰαθεὶς οὐκ ᾔδει τίς ἐστιν, ὁ γὰρ Ἰησοῦς ἐξένευσεν ὄχλου ὄντος ἐν τῷ τόπῳ.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] but having been healed not knew who it is, for the Jesus withdrew, a crowd being in the place.

en.L: But the one who had been healed did not know who it was, for Jesus had withdrawn, a crowd being in the place.
en.B: But the healed man had no idea who it was, since there was a crowd in the place and Jesus had moved off without being noticed.
en.R: But the man who had been healed did not know who had made him well. There were many people there, and Jesus had quietly left.

es.L: Pero el que había sido sanado no sabía quién era, porque Jesús se había retirado, habiendo mucha gente en el lugar.
es.B: Pero el hombre sanado no tenía idea de quién era, porque había mucha gente en el lugar y Jesús se había apartado sin que {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} notaran.
es.R: Pero el hombre que había sido sanado no sabía quién lo había sanado. Había mucha gente allí, y Jesús se había ido sin llamar la atención.

fr.L: Mais celui qui avait été guéri ne savait pas qui c’était, car Jésus s’était éclipsé, une foule se trouvant en ce lieu.
fr.B: Mais l’homme guéri ignorait qui c’était, car il y avait foule à cet endroit et Jésus s’était éloigné sans se faire remarquer.
fr.R: Mais l’homme qui avait été guéri ne savait pas qui l’avait guéri. Il y avait beaucoup de monde, et Jésus était parti discrètement.

sw.L: Lakini yule aliyeponywa hakumjua ni nani, kwa maana Yesu alikuwa amejitenga, kwa kuwa palikuwa na umati mahali pale.
sw.B: Lakini yule aliyeponywa hakujua ni nani, kwa kuwa palikuwa na umati mahali pale, na Yesu alikuwa ameondoka bila kuonekana.
sw.R: Lakini yule mtu aliyeponywa hakujua ni nani aliyemponya. Kulikuwa na watu wengi pale, na Yesu alikuwa ameondoka kimya kimya.

vi.L: Nhưng người được chữa lành không biết đó là ai, vì Đức Giê-xu đã lánh đi, vì có đám đông ở nơi đó.
vi.B: Nhưng người được chữa lành không biết đó là ai, vì chỗ ấy đông người và Đức Giê-xu đã lặng lẽ rời đi.
vi.R: Nhưng người được chữa lành không biết ai đã chữa cho mình. Ở đó có rất đông người, và Đức Giê-xu đã lặng lẽ rời đi.

ko.L: 그러나 고침을 받은 사람은 그가 누구인지 알지 못했다. 그곳에 무리가 있어서 예수께서 빠져나가셨기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그러나 병이 나은 사람은 그분이 누구인지 전혀 몰랐다. 그곳에 사람들이 많아서 예수께서 눈에 띄지 않게 빠져나가셨기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그러나 병이 나은 사람은 자기를 낫게 해 준 분이 누구인지 몰랐다. 그곳에는 사람들이 많았고, 예수께서는 조용히 그곳을 떠나셨다.

decisions.choice: withdrew: turned aside and slipped off
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn aside or withdraw. It is not used elsewhere in the New Testament, and it suggests leaving quietly rather than fleeing.

decisions.choice: a crowd being in the place: the crowd let Jesus leave unnoticed
alternatives: Jesus withdrew to avoid the crowd
decisions.reason: The phrase gives the circumstances of his leaving. Most naturally the crowd explains why the man lost sight of him; it may also suggest why Jesus left, to avoid attention. The two fit together, and neither changes what happened.

decisions.choice: the man did not know who Jesus was
decisions.reason: He had been healed without asking or believing first, and he did not even know his healer's name. Jesus finds him again in verse 14.

decisions.choice: moved off without being noticed (B); quietly left (R)
decisions.reason: Shows the sense of the verb and the part the crowd played (meaning decisions m1 and m2).

decisions.choice: se había apartado sin que lo notaran (B); se había ido sin llamar la atención (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: shows the sense of the verb and the part the crowd played (meaning decisions m1 and m2).

source.text: μετὰ ταῦτα εὑρίσκει αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἴδε ὑγιὴς γέγονας· μηκέτι ἁμάρτανε, ἵνα μὴ χεῖρόν σοί τι γένηται.

records.literal_gloss: After these things finds him the Jesus in the temple and said to him, "See, well you have become; no longer sin, that not worse to you something may happen."

en.L: After these things Jesus finds him in the temple and said to him, "See, you have become well; sin no longer, so that something worse may not happen to you."
en.B: Afterward Jesus found him in the temple area and said to him, "Look, you are well now. Do not sin any longer, or something worse could come upon you."
en.R: Later Jesus found the man in the temple courts. He said to him, "Look, you are well now. Do not go on sinning. If you do, something worse could happen to you."

es.L: Después de esto lo encuentra Jesús en el templo y le dijo: «Mira, has quedado sano; no peques más, para que no te suceda algo peor».
es.B: Más tarde Jesús lo encontró en los atrios del templo y le dijo: «Mira, ya estás sano. No peques más, no sea que te suceda algo peor».
es.R: Después Jesús encontró al hombre en el patio del templo y le dijo: «Mira, ya estás sano. No sigas pecando. Si lo haces, te podría pasar algo peor».

fr.L: Après ces choses, Jésus le trouve dans le temple et lui dit : « Vois, tu es devenu bien portant ; ne pèche plus, afin qu’il ne t’arrive pas quelque chose de pire. »
fr.B: Plus tard, Jésus le trouva dans la cour du temple et lui dit : « Te voilà guéri. Ne pèche plus, sinon il pourrait t’arriver quelque chose de pire. »
fr.R: Plus tard, Jésus a retrouvé l’homme dans la cour du temple. Il lui a dit : « Regarde, maintenant tu es guéri. Arrête de pécher. Sinon, il pourrait t’arriver quelque chose de pire. »

sw.L: Baadaye Yesu anamkuta katika hekalu, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akamwambia, "Angalia, umepata kuwa mzima; acha kutenda dhambi, ili jambo baya zaidi lisikupate."
sw.B: Baadaye Yesu alimkuta katika nyua za hekalu, akamwambia, "Angalia, sasa u mzima. Usiendelee kutenda dhambi, la sivyo jambo baya zaidi linaweza kukupata."
sw.R: Baadaye Yesu alimkuta yule mtu katika uwanja wa hekalu. Akamwambia, "Angalia, sasa umepona. Usiendelee kutenda dhambi. Ukiendelea, jambo baya zaidi linaweza kukupata."

vi.L: Sau những việc ấy, Đức Giê-xu gặp ông trong đền thờ và nói với ông: "Này, ông đã được lành; đừng phạm tội nữa, kẻo điều gì tệ hơn xảy đến cho ông."
vi.B: Sau đó Đức Giê-xu gặp ông ở sân đền thờ và nói: "Này, bây giờ ông đã được lành. Đừng phạm tội nữa, kẻo ông gặp điều còn tệ hơn."
vi.R: Sau đó, Đức Giê-xu tìm gặp ông ở sân đền thờ. Ngài nói với ông: "Này, bây giờ ông đã khỏe rồi. Đừng tiếp tục phạm tội nữa. Nếu không, điều tệ hơn có thể xảy đến cho ông."

ko.L: 그 후에 예수께서 성전에서 그를 찾아내신다. 그리고 그에게 말씀하셨다. "보아라, 네가 나았다. 더 나쁜 일이 너에게 생기지 않도록, 더 이상 죄를 짓지 마라."
ko.B: 얼마 뒤에 예수께서 성전 뜰에서 그를 찾아 만나시고 말씀하셨다. "보아라, 이제 네가 나았다. 더는 죄를 짓지 마라. 그러지 않으면 더 나쁜 일이 너에게 닥칠 수도 있다."
ko.R: 나중에 예수께서 성전 뜰에서 그 사람을 찾아 만나셨다. 예수께서 그에게 말씀하셨다. "보아라, 이제 너는 나았다. 이제는 죄를 짓지 마라. 죄를 계속 지으면 더 나쁜 일이 너에게 생길 수도 있다."

decisions.choice: stop sinning, so that nothing worse happens: a warning, not a statement that sin caused the illness
alternatives: the man's illness was a punishment for a particular sin
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say that the man's illness was caused by sin. In 9:2-3 he rejects the idea that a man's blindness came from his own sin or his parents'. Yet Scripture also speaks of sin that brings sickness in some cases (1 Corinthians 11:29-30; James 5:15-16), so the warning may suggest a link here without saying what it was. "Something worse" than thirty-eight years of illness is left unnamed; in the words that follow, Jesus speaks of judgment (5:24, 29).

decisions.choice: no longer sin: stop and do not go on
decisions.reason: The command is in a form that describes ongoing action, with "no longer": the man is not to continue in sin. The same words are spoken to the woman in 8:11.

decisions.choice: Jesus finds him: it is Jesus who seeks out the man
decisions.reason: As in 1:43 and 9:35, Jesus is the one who finds. The man did not know who had healed him (verse 13); Jesus comes to him again.

decisions.choice: the temple: the temple courts
decisions.reason: The word is the one for the whole temple area with its courts, where people gathered, not the sanctuary itself.

decisions.choice: temple area (B); temple courts (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for this word in John (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: See (L); Look (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Behold" is no longer everyday speech; the word calls attention to what has happened to him.

decisions.choice: los atrios del templo (B); el patio del templo (R)
decisions.reason: The choice made at 2:14 for this word, the whole temple area (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: le trouve ... et lui dit (L)
decisions.reason: John moves from the present ("finds") to the past ("said"); Literal keeps the present "trouve", and "dit" serves for both tenses in French, so the switch is gentler than in English. Balanced and Readable tell both in the past.

decisions.choice: "đền thờ" (L); "sân đền thờ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's choice for hieron, the whole temple area, as in docs/john-terms.md.

decisions.choice: "성전" (L); "성전 뜰" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As john-terms.md and the guide set for hieron: the whole temple area, where the man could be met, not the sanctuary itself.

decisions.choice: two sentences at Literal: "찾아내신다. 그리고 ... 말씀하셨다."
decisions.reason: The Greek puts "finds" in the present and "said" in the past; a Korean connective clause cannot carry its own tense, so Literal splits the sentence to keep both.

source.text: ἀπῆλθεν ὁ ἄνθρωπος καὶ ἀνήγγειλεν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ὅτι Ἰησοῦς ἐστιν ὁ ποιήσας αὐτὸν ὑγιῆ.

records.literal_gloss: Went away the man and reported to the Jews that Jesus is the [one] having made him well.

en.L: The man went away and reported to the Jews that it was Jesus who had made him well.
en.B: The man went off and told the Jewish leaders that the one who had made him well was Jesus.
en.R: The man went and told the Jewish leaders that it was Jesus who had healed him.

es.L: Se fue el hombre y anunció a los judíos que Jesús era el que lo había sanado.
es.B: El hombre se fue y les dijo a los dirigentes judíos que el que lo había sanado era Jesús.
es.R: El hombre fue y les dijo a los dirigentes judíos que Jesús era quien lo había sanado.

fr.L: L’homme s’en alla et annonça aux Juifs que c’était Jésus qui l’avait rendu bien portant.
fr.B: L’homme s’en alla dire aux chefs juifs que celui qui l’avait guéri, c’était Jésus.
fr.R: L’homme est allé dire aux chefs juifs que c’était Jésus qui l’avait guéri.

sw.L: Yule mtu aliondoka, akawajulisha Wayahudi kwamba ni Yesu ndiye aliyemfanya mzima.
sw.B: Yule mtu aliondoka, akawaambia viongozi wa Wayahudi kwamba aliyemfanya mzima ni Yesu.
sw.R: Yule mtu alikwenda akawaambia viongozi wa Wayahudi kwamba ni Yesu aliyemponya.

vi.L: Người ấy đi và báo cho người Do Thái biết rằng Đức Giê-xu là người đã chữa lành cho mình.
vi.B: Người ấy đi báo cho các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái biết rằng người đã chữa lành cho mình là Đức Giê-xu.
vi.R: Người ấy đi báo cho các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái biết chính Đức Giê-xu đã chữa bệnh cho mình.

ko.L: 그 사람은 가서, 자기를 낫게 한 이가 예수라고 유대인들에게 알렸다.
ko.B: 그 사람은 가서 유대 지도자들에게, 자기를 낫게 해 준 분이 예수라고 말했다.
ko.R: 그 사람은 가서 유대 지도자들에게, 자기를 고쳐 준 분이 예수라고 말했다.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the same authorities as in verses 10-13
decisions.reason: He goes back to those who had questioned him and answers their question of verse 12. The man himself is a Jew.

decisions.choice: reported: John does not say why the man told them
decisions.reason: The verb means to report or announce, and John uses it of making something known (4:25; 16:13-15). The man may have been clearing himself, or speaking up for his healer. John gives no motive, and the renderings give none.

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms). The footnote gives the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: healed him
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain word here; Literal and Balanced keep the phrase of verse 11.

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los dirigentes judíos (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the religious authorities (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable name them, as at 1:19 and 2:18. The word John wrote is "los judíos".

source.text: καὶ διὰ τοῦτο ἐδίωκον οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὅτι ταῦτα ἐποίει ἐν σαββάτῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And because of this were persecuting the Jews the Jesus, because these things he was doing on a Sabbath.

en.L: And because of this the Jews were persecuting Jesus, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was doing these things on a Sabbath.
en.B: For this reason the Jewish leaders began to persecute Jesus, since {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} kept doing such things on the Sabbath.
en.R: So the Jewish leaders began to go after Jesus, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was doing things like this on the Sabbath.

es.L: Y por esto los judíos perseguían a Jesús, porque hacía estas cosas en sábado.
es.B: Por esta razón los dirigentes judíos comenzaron a perseguir a Jesús, ya que hacía estas cosas en sábado.
es.R: Por eso los dirigentes judíos empezaron a ir contra Jesús, porque hacía cosas como esta en sábado.

fr.L: Et c’est pour cela que les Juifs persécutaient Jésus, parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} faisait ces choses un jour de sabbat.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi les chefs juifs se mirent à persécuter Jésus, parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} faisait ce genre de choses le jour du sabbat.
fr.R: Alors les chefs juifs ont commencé à s’en prendre à Jésus, parce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} faisait des choses comme cela le jour du sabbat.

sw.L: Na kwa ajili ya hilo Wayahudi walimfuatafuata Yesu kumtesa, kwa sababu alikuwa akiyafanya hayo siku ya Sabato.
sw.B: Kwa sababu hiyo viongozi wa Wayahudi walianza kumtesa Yesu, kwa kuwa aliendelea kufanya mambo kama hayo siku ya Sabato.
sw.R: Basi viongozi wa Wayahudi walianza kumwandama Yesu, kwa sababu alikuwa akifanya mambo kama hayo siku ya Sabato.

vi.L: Và vì điều này, người Do Thái bắt bớ Đức Giê-xu, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm những việc ấy trong ngày Sa-bát.
vi.B: Vì lý do đó, các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái bắt đầu bắt bớ Đức Giê-xu, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cứ làm những việc như thế trong ngày Sa-bát.
vi.R: Vì vậy, các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái bắt đầu tìm cách hại Đức Giê-xu, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm những việc như thế vào ngày Sa-bát.

ko.L: 그리고 이 때문에 유대인들이 예수를 박해하고 있었다. 그분이 안식일에 이런 일들을 하셨기 때문이다.
ko.B: 이런 까닭에 유대 지도자들은 예수를 박해하기 시작했다. 예수께서 안식일에 이런 일을 계속하셨기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그래서 유대 지도자들은 예수를 괴롭히기 시작했다. 예수께서 안식일에 이런 일을 하셨기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the religious authorities
decisions.reason: The same authorities as in verses 10-15, who now act against Jesus. It is not the people as a whole: Jesus, his disciples and the healed man are Jews.

decisions.choice: were persecuting: pursuing him as an offender
decisions.reason: The verb means to pursue, and so to harass or persecute. The imperfect shows an action begun and kept up. Verse 18 says what it led to: they wanted to kill him.

decisions.choice: these things he was doing: a habit, not one act
decisions.reason: The plural "these things" with an imperfect verb speaks of a practice. John tells of another Sabbath healing in chapter 9, and Jesus refers back to this one in 7:21-23.

decisions.choice: they persecuted Jesus (SBLGNT)
alternatives: "they persecuted Jesus and sought to kill him" (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "and they were seeking to kill him", as the King James Version reflects. The older manuscripts do not have it, and verse 18 says the same, so no footnote. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms). The footnote gives the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: began to persecute, kept doing (B); began to go after (R)
decisions.reason: Shows the beginning of an action that went on, and a habit of healing (meaning decisions m2 and m3); Readable uses plain words for "persecute".

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los dirigentes judíos (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the religious authorities (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable name them, as at 1:19 and 2:18. The word John wrote is "los judíos".

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀπεκρίνατο αὐτοῖς· Ὁ πατήρ μου ἕως ἄρτι ἐργάζεται κἀγὼ ἐργάζομαι.

records.literal_gloss: He but answered them, "The Father of me until now is working, and I am working."

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered them, "My Father is working until now, and I also am working."
en.B: Jesus answered them, "My Father has been at work right up to now, and I am at work as well."
en.R: Jesus answered them, "My Father is still working, right up to today, and I am working too."

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les respondió: «Mi Padre hasta ahora trabaja, y yo también trabajo».
es.B: Jesús les respondió: «Mi Padre sigue trabajando hasta ahora, y yo también trabajo».
es.R: Jesús les respondió: «Mi Padre sigue trabajando hasta hoy, y yo también trabajo».

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur répondit : « Mon Père est à l’œuvre jusqu’à maintenant, et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi, je suis à l’œuvre. »
fr.B: Jésus leur répondit : « Mon Père est à l’œuvre jusqu’à présent, et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi, je suis à l’œuvre. »
fr.R: Jésus leur a répondu : « Mon Père travaille encore, jusqu’à aujourd’hui, et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi, je travaille. »

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} akawajibu, "Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} anafanya kazi mpaka sasa, na mimi pia nafanya kazi."
sw.B: Yesu akawajibu, "Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} amekuwa akifanya kazi mpaka sasa, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} pia ninafanya kazi."
sw.R: Yesu akawajibu, "Baba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} bado anafanya kazi, mpaka leo, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} pia ninafanya kazi."

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đáp lại họ: "Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vẫn làm việc cho đến bây giờ, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng làm việc."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu trả lời họ: "Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vẫn làm việc cho đến tận bây giờ, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng đang làm việc."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu đáp: "Cha {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} vẫn đang làm việc cho đến tận hôm nay, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng làm việc."

ko.L: 그러나 그분이 그들에게 대답하셨다. "내 아버지께서 지금까지 일하고 계시고, 나도 일하고 있다."
ko.B: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "내 아버지께서는 지금까지 줄곧 일하고 계신다. 나도 일하고 있다."
ko.R: 예수께서 그들에게 대답하셨다. "내 아버지께서는 오늘까지도 계속 일하고 계신다. 그리고 나도 일하고 있다."

decisions.choice: God has never stopped working, on the Sabbath or any day
alternatives: God is working now, in this healing, only
decisions.reason: God rested on the seventh day from the work of creating (Genesis 2:2-3), yet he goes on giving life and upholding what he made (Psalm 104:27-30; 121:4). Philo of Alexandria, a Jewish writer of Jesus's lifetime, likewise says that God never ceases to work (Allegorical Interpretation 1.5-6). "Until now" means up to this very moment. If God is at work on the Sabbath, then the Son's work of giving life is not a breach of it (5:19-21).

decisions.choice: my Father: Jesus speaks of God as his own Father
alternatives: our Father, as any Israelite might say
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say "our Father" but "my Father", as in 2:16, and sets his own work beside the Father's. Verse 18 shows that his hearers understood what this claimed.

decisions.choice: and I too am working: the same verb, the same tense
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the same verb for himself as for the Father. His work is the Father's work carried on (5:19).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker, which the Greek leaves to the context.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} (L); My
decisions.reason: "My" at the start of the sentence is capitalized either way, so it is written plain.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}
decisions.reason: The stressed "él" for Jesus takes the setting; Balanced and Readable name him instead.

decisions.choice: être à l’œuvre (L, B); travailler (R)
decisions.reason: The same verb twice, in the same tense (meaning decision m3). "Être à l’œuvre" keeps the link with "les œuvres" the Father shows the Son (5:20, 5:36) and avoids the sense of a paid job; Readable uses the plain verb "travailler" for both.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} aussi
decisions.reason: English "I" needs no span, but French puts the stressed pronoun "moi" before "je" to render the Greek "I too"; as a pronoun for Christ it takes the deity_pronoun setting.

source.text: διὰ τοῦτο οὖν μᾶλλον ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀποκτεῖναι ὅτι οὐ μόνον ἔλυε τὸ σάββατον, ἀλλὰ καὶ πατέρα ἴδιον ἔλεγε τὸν θεόν, ἴσον ἑαυτὸν ποιῶν τῷ θεῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Because of this therefore more were seeking him the Jews to kill, because not only he was loosing the Sabbath, but also Father own he was calling the God, equal himself making to the God.

en.L: Because of this, therefore, the Jews were seeking all the more to kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} not only was breaking the Sabbath, but also was calling God {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own Father, making {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} equal to God.
en.B: So the Jewish leaders were even more determined to kill {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Besides breaking the Sabbath, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking of God as {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own Father, and so was making {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} equal to God.
en.R: Because of this the Jewish leaders tried even harder to find a way to kill Jesus. He was breaking the Sabbath, and more than that, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was calling God {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own Father. That meant {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was making {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} equal with God.

es.L: Por esto, pues, los judíos buscaban aún más matarlo, porque no solo quebrantaba el sábado, sino que también llamaba a Dios {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio Padre, haciéndose igual a Dios.
es.B: Por eso los dirigentes judíos estaban aún más decididos a matarlo. Además de quebrantar el sábado, llamaba a Dios {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio Padre, y así se hacía igual a Dios.
es.R: Por eso los dirigentes judíos buscaban con más ganas la manera de matar a Jesús. No solo violaba la ley del sábado, sino que además llamaba a Dios {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propio Padre. Eso significaba que se hacía igual a Dios.

fr.L: C’est donc pour cela que les Juifs cherchaient d’autant plus à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire mourir, parce que non seulement {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} violait le sabbat, mais encore {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} nommait Dieu {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre Père, se faisant {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} égal à Dieu.
fr.B: Les chefs juifs n’en furent que plus décidés à {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire mourir. En plus de violer le sabbat, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} parlait de Dieu comme de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre Père, et se faisait ainsi {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} égal à Dieu.
fr.R: À cause de cela, les chefs juifs cherchaient encore plus un moyen de tuer Jésus. Il ne respectait pas le sabbat, et, plus grave encore, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} appelait Dieu {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} propre Père. Cela voulait dire qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se faisait {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} égal à Dieu.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo, kwa sababu hii Wayahudi waliongeza juhudi za kumtafuta ili wamwue; si kwa kuwa aliivunja Sabato tu, bali pia alikuwa akisema kwamba Mungu ni Baba {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} mwenyewe, akijiweka sawa na Mungu.
sw.B: Basi viongozi wa Wayahudi wakazidi kuazimia kumwua. Mbali na kuivunja Sabato, alikuwa akisema kwamba Mungu ni Baba {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} mwenyewe, na hivyo alikuwa akijifanya sawa na Mungu.
sw.R: Kwa sababu hiyo viongozi wa Wayahudi walijitahidi zaidi kutafuta njia ya kumwua Yesu. Alikuwa akiivunja Sabato, na zaidi ya hayo, alikuwa akimwita Mungu Baba {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} mwenyewe. Maana yake ni kwamba alikuwa akijifanya sawa na Mungu.

vi.L: Vì thế người Do Thái lại càng tìm cách giết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hơn nữa, vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không những phá bỏ ngày Sa-bát, mà còn gọi Đức Chúa Trời là Cha của chính mình, tự làm mình ngang bằng với Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.B: Vì vậy, các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái càng quyết tâm giết {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hơn. Không những {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vi phạm ngày Sa-bát, mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} còn gọi Đức Chúa Trời là Cha của riêng mình, và như thế là tự cho mình ngang hàng với Đức Chúa Trời.
vi.R: Vì thế, các nhà lãnh đạo Do Thái càng tìm cách giết Đức Giê-xu hơn nữa. Ngài đã vi phạm ngày Sa-bát, mà hơn thế nữa, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} còn gọi Đức Chúa Trời là Cha của riêng mình. Như vậy là {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} tự cho mình ngang hàng với Đức Chúa Trời.

ko.L: 이 때문에 유대인들은 더욱더 그분을 죽이려고 했다. 그분이 안식일을 어기셨을 뿐 아니라, 하나님을 자기 아버지라고 부르셔서 자신을 하나님과 동등하게 만드셨기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그래서 유대 지도자들은 더욱 예수를 죽이려고 했다. 예수께서 안식일을 어기셨을 뿐 아니라, 하나님을 자기 아버지라고 하셔서 자신을 하나님과 동등한 자리에 두셨기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그래서 유대 지도자들은 예수를 죽일 방법을 더욱 애써 찾았다. 예수께서는 안식일을 어기셨고, 그보다 더한 것은 하나님을 자기 아버지라고 부르신 것이었다. 그것은 자신을 하나님과 같은 분으로 만드는 일이었다.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the religious authorities
decisions.reason: The same authorities as in verses 10-16, now seeking his death (also 7:1, 19, 25). Not the people as a whole.

decisions.choice: breaking the Sabbath: treating it as not binding
decisions.reason: The verb means to loosen or undo, and so to break or set aside a law; John uses it so in 7:23 and 10:35. This was the charge as the authorities saw it. Jesus has answered it in verse 17, and answers it again in 7:21-23: his work is the Father's work.

decisions.choice: his own Father: claiming God as Father in a unique way
alternatives: Father in the sense any Israelite could use
decisions.reason: Israel could call God its Father (Isaiah 63:16; 64:8). The word "own" marks the difference: Jesus spoke of God as Father in a way that belonged to him alone, and set his work beside God's (verse 17).

decisions.choice: making himself equal to God: how the authorities understood his claim
alternatives: a claim Jesus made to be a second god
decisions.reason: John records their conclusion. He does not deny that Jesus is equal to God: the Word was God (1:1), and all are to honor the Son as they honor the Father (5:23). What the next verses deny is that the Son makes himself anything on his own: he does nothing of himself, but only what he sees the Father doing (5:19, 30). Compare Philippians 2:6.

decisions.choice: all the more: they were already set against him
decisions.reason: "All the more" looks back to verse 16: their hostility, already begun, grows into a settled wish to kill him. The imperfect shows them going on seeking it.

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms). The footnote gives the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: two sentences (B: Besides ... ; R: He was ... and more than that ...)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the sentence and keep the build-up of "not only ... but also": the second charge is the graver one.

decisions.choice: That meant
decisions.reason: Readable spells out how the last phrase relates to the one before: calling God his own Father amounted to making himself equal with God (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los dirigentes judíos (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the religious authorities (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable name them, as at 1:19 and 2:18. The word John wrote is "los judíos".

decisions.choice: Eso significaba que
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable spells out how the last phrase relates to the one before (meaning decision m4).
